name: Resupply allies
summary: A unit gives teammates back what they have used up: ammunition, fuel, energy or ability charges. It drops a crate or pack that refills everyone standing near it, parks a supply vehicle beside them, hands a pouch to one ally, or lands a buff that reloads whoever it touches. The supplier works from a limited stock of its own, or pays with a cooldown, money or a spent minion. It only matters where supplies are scarce: units on a finite stock, slow-reloading heavy weapons, grenades and gadgets. The supplier is soft, tends to sit still while it works and is a prime target; in some games its crate serves enemies too, or the whole vehicle can be captured.
counterplay: Kill the supplier: it is soft and often parked, and the heavy weapons in front of it run dry soon after.
Destroy the crate, or use it yourself where it serves anyone who stands near it (PlanetSide 2's ammo pack, Battlefield 2142's ammo hub).
Cut the route: a supplier with a limited stock has to go back to a base to restock, so raid the road or the base behind it.
Make them spend: draw out rockets, shells and grenades with feints and cover, then push while they wait at the crate.
Splash the queue: teammates bunch up around a crate, a truck or a landing pad.
Where the game allows it, surround a supply vehicle and take it: in Wargame it gives up and changes sides.

other_examples.unit: Supply trucks, supply helicopters and the FOB
other_examples.note: These units carry a limited stock of supply points, shown as a bar on the unit, and spend it to refuel, re-arm and mend whatever is parked near them; each of the three services can be switched off to save the stock for the others. They must sit still on the ground to work, restock at the forward base (which drains that base in turn) and are soft targets that artillery hunts. Trucks are cheap and easy to hide; helicopters carry far more but can't be hidden. A supply vehicle ringed by enemies gives up and changes sides until it is retaken.

other_examples.unit: Fuel, the air staging facility and carriers
other_examples.note: Fuel is the stock that gets refilled: aircraft burn it as they fly and, once it is gone, crawl along as easy prey instead of crashing. It creeps back while they sit on the ground and returns at once when they dock on an air staging platform, a carrier or the Fatboy mobile factory. The platform also repairs them, aircraft low on fuel or health fly back by themselves, and with few pads the queue to dock is the real limit. On big maps the mobile carriers bring the pad close to the front.

sources.title: Air staging facility, Supreme Commander Wiki

shooter_analogues.unit: Ammo Box and Ammo Bag (Support kit)
shooter_analogues.note: Since Battlefield 2 the Support kit carries ammo bags or boxes as a gadget and scores points for the teammates it supplies; the carrier's own boxes come back with time, and each kit keeps just one crate out. A Battlefield 2 bag held close to teammates tops them up bit by bit, or thrown down it restocks in full whoever crosses it. Battlefield 3's box refills magazines fast, explosives more slowly and grenades slowest of all, to curb grenade spam; several boxes speed each other up, and a box tossed onto a vehicle makes a moving supply point.

sources.title: Ammo Box, Battlefield Wiki
sources.note: Its quote boxes copy the in-game and Battlelog descriptions of the Battlefield 2 ammo bag and the Battlefield 3 ammo box.

shooter_analogues.note: On a key the Engineer throws a pack a short way; it lies there for a set time and keeps refilling the foot soldiers and power-armoured suits around it, quickly for most guns and far more slowly for rocket launchers. It serves anyone standing near it, enemies included, although a pack shows on the minimap for its own side alone. Upgrades make it last longer and reach wider, and the top rank allows two at once.

sources.title: Ammunition Package, PlanetSide 2 Wiki
sources.version: Marked current as of the 26 May 2021 hotfix

shooter_analogues.note: A building the Engineer puts up that gives everyone on his team who stands near it ammunition and health without end, plus a small, slowly refilling stock of building metal for Engineers; enemy Spies in disguise can use it too. It can't defend itself and takes time and metal to build and upgrade, each level giving more. Teammates gather round it, which anchors a position and also turns them into one target for splash.

The far end of the scale, where supply is a whole player job: players gather raw resources, refine them, turn them into crates of weapons and ammunition at factories and haul the crates to bases at the front or to depots. The front fights with what the haulers bring, and the better-supplied side has a large edge.

A refill added to a support zone: with these boots on, the rifts a Warlock places also make the wearer and any allies standing inside reload much faster. The boots have to be worn at the moment the rift is cast.

sources.title: Lunafaction Boots, Destiny Wiki
sources.note: The perk box gives the text of the armour's perk, Alchemical Etchings.

player_translation.summary: A supplier keeps the team's guns fed: drop a crate that gives ammo, gadgets and ability charges back to everyone standing near it, or park a supply vehicle behind the push. It matters wherever ammo is scarce, and the crate becomes a spot both teams fight over.
as_user: You buy a support unit that carries supplies as well as a weapon: press Q to drop a crate, and teammates inside its small ring get ammo, grenades and ability charges back over a few seconds.
You choose where the supply goes: behind cover near the fight, beside the tank that has fired off its shells, or on the route teammates fall back along.
Your own stock is limited: the crate is on a cooldown, or you carry a few and restock at base, so each drop is a decision.
You score for every refill a teammate takes from you, so the job pays even when you fire little.
As a supply vehicle you park and teammates come to you, and you are a soft, still target while you work.
as_target: You see the crate and its ring; destroy it and the enemy's refills stop.
Kill the supplier and the heavy weapons in front of it run dry within a fight or two.
Count shots: a unit on a finite stock that has emptied it far from a crate is weak until it gets back.
In the open-crate variant you can stand in an enemy crate and take its ammo yourself.
teammates: Players on finite ammo, such as rocket troops, artillery and gadget-heavy kits, stay near the supplier or call it over with a ping.
The crate turns a piece of cover into a small forward base that the team holds.
Units built to be fed by teammates get their burst back when the supplier arrives.
On the enemy side, raiders and artillery hunt the crate and the supplier; that is how a dug-in team is starved out.
controls: Move with WASD and aim with the mouse; press Q to drop the crate at your feet, or hold Q to place it at the cursor within a short range.
For the hand-off version, aim at one teammate and tap Q to throw them a pouch.
A supply vehicle deploys with Q: parked, it serves everyone in its ring, and it can't supply while moving.
Middle mouse, the universal ping: teammates call for ammo and the supplier marks where the crate is.
feedback: The crate shows a team-coloured ring and a gauge of what it has left; teammates inside see their ammo counters tick up, with a soft sound.
Teammates low on ammo show an ammo icon to suppliers, on screen and on the minimap.
The supplier's HUD shows crates left or the cooldown, and counts the refills given.
Enemies see a spotted crate as a marked object and hear it being placed.
changes_from_rts: Most RTS units never run out of ammo. The pattern needs a game where some weapons do (finite stocks, slow magazines, grenades, ability charges), or it has nothing to give.
Wargame's supply trucks serve whatever is parked beside them without an order; a player needs a clear loop of placing and scoring, so the crate and the points per refill come from shooters.
Wargame's supply is a slow strategic stock hauled from a forward base; in a short match a cooldown or a small carried stock replaces the long haul.

In Tempest Rising the refill rides on a buff that also protects and speeds up, given by a thrall's sacrifice or by a blessing paid in credits. Here the plain crate stands alone, and the refill carried by a buff is a variant.
Refill bullets fast and explosives slowly, as Battlefield 3 does, so a crate does not turn into endless rocket or grenade spam.

team_play.notes: The supplier lets teammates on scarce ammo stay at the front, and its crate or truck becomes a small base the team gathers at and the enemy raids. How much it matters depends on how scarce ammo is in the game: where nothing runs dry, nobody needs it.

notes: It presumes an ammo economy: some weapons, gadgets or abilities must run on a stock that can run out.
A crate entity with health, a ring, a lifetime and a refill tick per weapon type; slower rates for explosives.
Stock rules for the supplier: a cooldown, or carried crates restocked at base.
Score for refills, low-ammo icons for suppliers and the ping pair.
Variants add a deployable vehicle mode, a built station or a pad that aircraft dock on.
Free ammo removes the limit that keeps rockets, grenades and artillery in check; refill explosives slowly and cap the crate's stock.
If nothing in the game runs short of ammo, the pick is dead weight; if everything does, the supplier becomes a must-pick.
A team camped on a crate in good cover can be very hard to shift; give the crate modest health and a lifetime.
Several crates on one spot should not multiply the refill rate without a cap.
A crate with a ring is easy to read from above; show its remaining stock so both teams know when it is spent.
Enemies need a cue that a unit has just been refilled, or a shot count they kept goes wrong.

variants.name: Dropped crate
variants.summary: Drop a crate or pack that lies on the ground for a while and refills everyone standing near it.
variants.seen_in: Battlefield Ammo Box; PlanetSide 2 Ammunition Package

variants.name: Hand-off
variants.summary: Throw a pouch to one teammate for a quick refill, or hold the bag close to top them up bit by bit: faster and more mobile than a crate, but for one ally at a time.

variants.name: Supply vehicle
variants.summary: A truck or helicopter carries a large but finite stock, has to park to hand it out and must drive back to base to restock; it is soft and worth hunting.
variants.seen_in: Wargame supply trucks and helicopters; Foxhole logistics trucks

variants.name: Built station
variants.summary: Put up a fixed dispenser that supplies without end while it stands; it takes time to build, can't defend itself and gathers the team around one spot.

variants.name: Docking pad
variants.summary: The unit is a pad: aircraft or drones land on it to refuel and rearm at once, a few at a time, so a mobile carrier brings the pad to the front.
variants.seen_in: Supreme Commander air staging facility and aircraft carriers

variants.name: Refill carried by a buff
variants.summary: No crate: the supplier's buff or support zone reloads whoever it lands on, or makes them reload and recharge faster while they stand in it.
variants.seen_in: Tempest Rising Enlightened (Sacrifice) and Vimana (Sacrificial Benediction); Destiny 2 Lunafaction Boots

variants.name: Open crate
variants.summary: The crate serves anyone who stands near it, enemies included, so where it is dropped matters and a lost position feeds the other side.
variants.seen_in: PlanetSide 2 Ammunition Package; Battlefield 2142 Ammo Hub

adds_strengths.why: Keeps teammates' heavy weapons, grenades and gadgets topped up at the front, so they need not go back to base.

adds_weaknesses.why: Its own stock or cooldown limits it, and it is soft and often standing still beside the crate or parked to hand out supplies.

countered_by.why: Fast flankers reach the supplier and its crate behind the line and cut the refills off.
Artillery shells a parked supplier or a crate from beyond the fight.
Teammates bunch up around the crate, and area damage hits them all.

open_questions: Is ammo scarce anywhere in Shamble Frontlines? Which weapons would run on a finite stock or a slow magazine, and do ability charges count as something to refill?
Is the crate on a cooldown, or does the supplier carry a few and restock at base?
May enemies use a crate they stand in, as in PlanetSide 2, or can they only destroy it?
Should explosives refill more slowly than bullets, as in Battlefield 3?
Is ammo support its own pick, or one more tool on the unit that repairs and heals?

shooter_fit.reason: A staple support job in team shooters (Battlefield's ammo box, PlanetSide 2's ammo pack, the TF2 Dispenser), and a crate with a ring reads well from above. It earns its place only if some weapons in the game can run dry.
